problem: Whether the variance alone forces a lower bound of order 1/V on the normalized Turán deficit of a Poisson–binomial pmf near its mode, and with what constant, at the first index D where the pmf decreases.
debate: Quantitative strengthenings of log-concavity and ultra-log-concavity for Bernoulli sums (Newton and Pitman, Hillion–Johnson, Johnson, Dümbgen–Wellner, Darroch on mode location, and the maximal-mass bounds of Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne), though no named controversy is stated.
gap: Known lower bounds on the Turán deficit depend on n, on the success probabilities, or on k alone, and so degenerate at fixed variance when many summands have p_i near 0 or 1, while mode-location and maximal-mass results give no lower bound on the deficit.
contribution: A proof that V*delta_D >= 1/4 for V >= 1, an explicit binomial family showing no constant above 1/3 is possible, corollaries at every k and at the rightmost mode, and a Haar-unitary half-circle example, all via cubic inequalities plus a one-variable inequality proved in exact arithmetic by Bernstein expansions.
note: The problem, gap and result are clear and the 1/4 versus 1/3 gap is honest, but the opening never says who needs a variance-scaled Turán bound at the first descent beyond the unitary example, so state the use before a referee asks.
